# sbox Network Storage Server

> Open-source, self-hosted s&box game backend using the existing Network Storage client library. This file is a documentation index, not a separate API specification.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): Linux VPS quickstart, HTTPS tunnel opt-in, project/public-key setup, security model, game values, editor secret key and Base URL, YAML definition sync, owner console, preview caveats and CLI reference.
- [Self-hosting](docs/self-hosting.md): Linux/macOS, Windows, Docker, manual installation, services, HTTPS, optional tunnel/email/telemetry and backups.
- [Client setup](docs/client-setup.md): Connect the s&box editor and game to a self-hosted Base URL; distinguish syncing definitions from moving runtime player records.
- [Hosting models](docs/hosting-models.md): Player-hosted, dedicated and hybrid games; where authority lives and which key each caller uses.
- [Game-client protocol](docs/game-client.md): Startup handshakes performed by the library.
- [Game-client protocol](docs/game-client.md) route root: released libraries call `/v3/{path}`; `/v3/{path}` and `/api/v3/{path}` are the permanent surface for existing methods and endpoints; new features are `/api/{path}` only, and `/api/{path}` mirrors existing non-reserved `/v3` families. `/api/storage` follows `x-ns-library-version` (`1.2.0` or newer uses the canonical v3 handlers; missing, malformed or older keeps legacy). The library default `/api` is planned (counterpart #36, not shipped).
- [Game values](docs/game-values.md): Shared tuning numbers; owner/API/MCP authoring and Sync Tool YAML source compilation in current source (release 0.5.4 lacks the fix); one-call reads; snapshots require explicit revision policy, retained support, and may fall back to live for missing resources; worked anti-exploit example.

## Operators and coding agents

- [MCP](docs/mcp.md): stdio tools for coding agents (setup, YAML definitions, dry runs, logs, errors, records), SSH setup, opt-in write permissions, and the Claude Code plugin in `agent-plugin/`.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): TOML settings, defaults, environment overrides and secrets.
- [Databases](docs/database.md): SQLite/PostgreSQL storage, schema isolation and database administration.
- [Owner dashboard](docs/admin-panel.md): Local-owner setup/sign-in, projects, keys, settings, schema-validated record mutations, resource authoring, runtime diagnostics and single-project migration.
- [Export and import](docs/export.md): Portable server archives, secret inclusion and restore constraints.
- [Alerting](docs/alerting.md): Notification channels (SMTP, Discord, signed webhooks and presets), captured-error alerts and shared limits.
- [Monitoring](docs/monitoring.md): Server page live stats, alert rules over host and request metrics, sampling cost and history.

## Official client and authoring references

These references also describe the managed service. Use repository guides for self-hosted installation and operation; managed billing, package tiers and the default API hostname are not self-hosting requirements.

- [Install the s&box library](https://sbox.game/sboxcool/network-storage): Official library package.
- [Client source](https://github.com/sbox-cool/sbox-network-storage): C# client and editor integration source.
- [Network Storage v3 documentation](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3): Official documentation index.
- [Library setup](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3/getting-started/library-setup): Install and configure the game client.
- [Library reference](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3/getting-started/library-reference): C# API reference.
- [YAML Source authoring](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3/core-concepts/source-authoring): Resource formats; YAML definitions are distinct from JSON runtime requests and responses.
- [Sync Tool](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3/security-production/sync-tools): Editor resource authoring and push/pull workflows.
- [Code examples](https://sboxcool.com/wiki/network-storage-v3/code-examples): Game systems and authored resource examples.
